items.summary: A 10,000 Birds post with photographs of two monarch flycatcher species seen in Raja Ampat, off West Papua in Indonesia, including the Frilled Monarch. The writer notes that its genus name, Arses, comes from the name of two ancient Persian kings.

items.title: Bruinisse, the Zeeland village that built a boulevard for its mussels
items.why: Some towns get a statue of a founder; Bruinisse got a giant opened mussel at the end of a dyke-top promenade. The village has lived off the mussel beds for centuries and its fleet still sails daily in season. If you ever find yourself in Zeeland between July and April, you know what's for dinner.
items.summary: Bruinisse, on the edge of Zeeland in the Netherlands, celebrates the mussel farming that has supported it for centuries. Its harbour holds an active mussel fleet, and a Mussel Boulevard along the protective dyke ends at a large artwork shaped like an open mussel.

items.title: Sem86, an x86 emulator that reads its instruction semantics from a file
items.why: Most emulators bake every instruction's behaviour into the code; Sem86 loads it at runtime, so you can swap in a different idea of what an opcode does, undocumented corners and all. Despite going through LLVM instead of a hand-tuned JIT it outruns Bochs. The long game, cloning a real CPU's behaviour by inferring it automatically, is wonderfully ambitious.
items.summary: Sem86 is a full-system x86 emulator that takes instruction semantics from an input file instead of hardcoding them, making it easy to model undefined behaviour and undocumented instructions. Its authors report it runs about twice as fast as Bochs and at roughly 42 percent of QEMU's speed, and they plan to feed it semantics inferred automatically by their libLISA project.

items.title: Marc Brooker looks back on seven years of Firecracker
items.why: Firecracker was the moment a lot of people realised a VMM could be small enough to boot per request and still keep tenants properly apart. Brooker revisits it from the inside, years after the NSDI paper, with the benefit of hindsight on what the design bought Lambda. Light on marketing, heavy on why.
items.summary: Marc Brooker reflects on seven years since AWS open-sourced Firecracker, the lightweight virtual machine monitor behind Lambda, first shown at re:Invent 2018. He revisits the 2020 NSDI paper on the design and looks at how its use and thinking have evolved since.

items.title: Five out-of-print SF collections from the disco era
items.why: James Davis Nicoll answers the perennial newcomer question with a straight face: what's good and recent, where recent means fifty-odd years ago. Short story collections from the 60s and 70s are where a lot of the era's best ideas actually lived, and most are now hard to find. A reading list for second-hand bookshop rummaging.
items.summary: Reactor columnist James Davis Nicoll picks five out-of-print short story collections by science fiction writers who were new and exciting in the 1960s and 70s. The Best of Walter M. Miller, Jr. is among them.

items.title: Sekka Zusetsu, an Edo-era book of snowflakes seen through a microscope
items.why: Decades before photomicrography, a Japanese feudal lord sat with a Dutch-style microscope and drew snow crystals one by one. The results became a pattern book that turned up on kimono and lacquerware. Lovely, and a nice reminder that the Western science story is not the only one.
items.summary: The Public Domain Review presents Sekka Zusetsu, an 1832 Japanese book of snow crystal observations made through a microscope by the daimyo Doi Toshitsura. Its drawings of these snow flowers went on to inspire decorative designs in Edo-period Japan.

items.title: An inkjet printer, caught mid-splash, among this year's photomicrography winners
items.why: Small-scale photography competitions always deliver, and one of this year's standouts is a composite of a printhead spitting ink onto paper. The photographer had to reverse the mechanism, moving the paper instead of the head, just to get a lens close enough. Hardware hacking in the service of a pretty picture.
items.summary: Kottke highlights winners of the 2026 photomicrography competition, including Ole Bielfeldt's image of an inkjet printer depositing droplets on paper. Because the droplets fly at around 20 metres per second, he built a custom rig in which the paper moved beneath a stationary printhead.

items.title: Euclid Space Telescope Releases First Massive Data Batch
items.why: The ESA's Euclid mission has dropped its first major data release, bringing us significantly closer to a comprehensive 3D map of the universe. For anyone tracking cosmological structures and dark matter research, this is a treasure chest of new observations.
items.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid Space Telescope has published its initial large-scale dataset captured by its 600-megapixel camera. The mission aims to chart the largest 3D map of the universe to better understand dark energy and dark matter.

items.title: Asteroid Bennu Samples Deliver Fresh Prebiotic Surprises
items.why: Comparing asteroid return samples with known meteorites using atomic-level isotope techniques gives researchers a sharper window into the early solar system. It is a fantastic look at how organic precursors to life formed across different parts of the protoplanetary disk.
items.summary: Researchers analyzing samples from asteroid Bennu alongside the Murchison meteorite have measured individual atomic isotope differences within the amino acid beta-alanine. The results indicate that some prebiotic building blocks formed under varying conditions in the early solar system.

items.title: Designing Azure Silicon on Custom ARM Hardware
items.why: Eating your own dog food reaches an extreme scale when a cloud provider uses its own custom ARM processors to simulate and verify future silicon chips. It is a neat look at the heavy electronic design automation workloads required to build modern infrastructure.
items.summary: Microsoft is sharing early results from running electronic design automation workloads for its custom chips on Azure Cobalt 200 hardware. The massive simulation and verification jobs account for hundreds of millions of compute tasks annually.

items.title: Finding Developer Fixes Hiding in AI Agent Trajectories
items.why: Passing an evaluation score doesn't tell you why an automated assistant struggled with a coding task, making step-by-step trajectory logs invaluable for engineering improvements. This is a practical reality check for anyone building reliable agent workflows.
items.dept: from the trace log troubleshooting dept.
items.summary: A deep dive into agent evaluation shows that final test scores often hide how many times an assistant stumbled before succeeding. Analyzing the complete trajectory of every step an agent takes provides the necessary insights to improve developer tooling.

items.title: Modernizing a Classic TRS-80 Color Computer with an FPGA
items.why: Retrocomputing hardware mods rarely get more invasive or impressive than giving a vintage 1980s machine an entire system architecture upgrade via modern programmable logic. It is a brilliant piece of engineering nostalgia for anyone who loves old iron.
items.summary: A hardware enthusiast has designed a Tang Nano 20K FPGA board modification that brings modern memory expansion, HDMI output, and enhanced sound to the classic Radio Shack TRS-80 Colour Computer 3.

items.title: First Look at the Askar N160 Ultra-Fast Newtonian Reflector
items.why: Finding a portable telescope that balances a generous aperture with a fast focal ratio without needing a monstrous mount is always a win for backyard astrophotographers. Real-world testing notes offer a grounded perspective on new imaging gear.
items.summary: A first-hand review of the Askar N160 highlights its performance as a compact, ultra-fast 160mm Newtonian reflector designed to provide high light-gathering power for backyard deep-sky imaging.

items.title: Hubble and Roman Team Up on Gravitational Lenses
items.why: Gravitational lenses offer some of the best tools for studying dark matter and galactic evolution across cosmic time. Combining Hubble's archival sharpness with the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope gives astronomers an incredible multi-mission observational pipeline.
items.summary: A new gallery of strong gravitational lenses captured by the Hubble Space Telescope highlights targets that will be revisited by the newly launched Roman Space Telescope. These cosmic magnifying glasses help scientists investigate dark matter distribution and the evolution of distant galaxies.

items.title: Saturn Hidden Behind the Lunar Limb
items.why: Occultations provide a rare dynamic moment when observing the outer planets against familiar lunar features. This image captures the quiet precision of planetary tracking and amateur-professional astrophotography at its best.
items.summary: A stunning astrophotography shot captures Saturn disappearing behind the lit limb of Earth's Moon during an occultation event. Such alignments offer a rare perspective on the relative motion of bodies in our inner and outer solar system.

items.title: Modernizing .NET Apps for Windows Arm64 with GitHub Copilot
items.why: Moving legacy enterprise workloads to Arm architecture usually involves tracking down hundreds of hidden dependency blockers and build settings. Using an AI assistant to plan and execute that migration saves developers countless hours of manual audit work.
items.summary: The GitHub Copilot upgrade agent now helps developers assess and modernize existing .NET applications for migration to Windows Arm64. The tool identifies platform blockers, builds a migration plan, and updates code and configuration dependencies automatically.

items.title: Tiny Solar-Powered Transmitters Track Monarch Butterfly Migration
items.why: Weighing in at just 60 milligrams with zero batteries, these custom Bluetooth tags represent an astonishing feat of biological telemetry. It is a brilliant hardware hack connecting tiny garden visitors to modern mobile location services.
items.summary: Researchers are using a 60-milligram solar-powered Bluetooth transmitter attached with eyelash glue to track the incredible migration of monarch butterflies. The featherlight tags allow scientists and citizen scientists alike to follow the insects using standard smartphone location services.

items.title: Porting Elite to the Commodore PET
items.why: Porting a legendary open-world game to a machine with strictly block graphics four decades later is pure hacker joy. It showcases a deep appreciation for classical 6502 assembly constraints and retro systems.
items.summary: Developer David Given has successfully ported the iconic 1980s open-world space trading game Elite to the Commodore PET. Running on a 6502 processor with 32k of memory, the port relies on the PET's block graphics rather than modern high-resolution displays.

items.title: NGC 4449: The Small Galaxy Punching Above Its Weight
items.why: Dwarf galaxies often harbor intense starburst activity that rivals much larger spirals, providing crucial laboratories for stellar formation. This NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day highlights the surprising ferocity of small cosmic systems.
items.summary: A detailed look at the dwarf irregular galaxy NGC 4449 reveals a widespread, frantic wave of active star formation. Despite being a fraction of the size of the Milky Way, this small galaxy is currently manufacturing stars at an astonishing rate.

items.title: Chandra Unmasks a Supernova Impostor
items.why: Distinguishing between cataclysmic stellar deaths and recurring outbursts from unstable massive stars is notoriously difficult. Finding a compact binary companion behind the outbursts solves a long-standing astronomical mystery.
items.summary: New research using the Chandra X-Ray Observatory reveals that a periodic 'supernova impostor' star outburst is actually powered by a binary relationship with a black hole or neutron star. Luminous Blue Variables often mimic true supernovae, but their recurring flares point to complex stellar interactions.

items.title: What Happens When Asteroid Mining Hits the Market?
items.why: Discussions of space mining usually focus on the rocketry and engineering rather than the macroeconomic reality. Applying system dynamics to platinum market shocks provides a grounded look at future space industry economics.
items.summary: A pair of system dynamicists from MIT have modeled the economic impact of harvesting platinum-group metals from asteroids using spacecraft like AstroForge. Their research suggests that while asteroid mining would crash rare-earth commodity prices, the broader industrial availability would benefit Earth immensely.

items.title: The Ice Giants' Strange and Shifting Magnetic Fields
items.why: Uranus and Neptune have long puzzled astronomers with magnetic fields that bear little resemblance to Earth's orderly dipole. New modeling suggests these chaotic fields may change on surprisingly short timescales compared to our last visit from Voyager 2. It is a fascinating look at the dynamic interiors of the solar system's ice giants.
items.summary: New research suggests that the messy, tilted magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune may change on very short timescales, potentially looking quite different than they did during Voyager 2's flybys in the 1980s. These findings highlight how little we still know about the unique interiors of our solar system's ice giants.

items.title: Seestar S30 Plus Review: A New Entry-Level Smart Telescope
items.why: Smart telescopes are rapidly transforming how backyard astronomers capture deep-sky objects without spending a fortune. This review of the Seestar S30 Plus offers a realistic look at what an affordable, app-controlled 30mm apochromatic setup can achieve for beginners.
items.summary: The Seestar S30 Plus bridges the gap between ultra-portable smart scopes and traditional astrophotography gear with a $499 price tag. Featuring a 30mm aperture and dual cameras, it gives beginners an accessible way to image deep-sky targets from the backyard.

items.title: Data Shows Used EV Batteries Are Holding Up Better Than Expected
items.why: Skepticism around battery longevity has been a persistent talking point for electric vehicles, but empirical data tells a much more encouraging story. Diagnostic testing from hundreds of thousands of real-world vehicles provides valuable insight into actual degradation rates over time.
items.summary: Analysis of more than 500,000 battery tests across popular electric vehicle models reveals that packs are degrading far more slowly than critics anticipated. Diagnostics companies utilizing rapid OBD tests are finding that used EV batteries retain health much better than feared.

items.title: Modular, 3D-Printed Train Whistles for Your Inner Conductor
items.why: There is something inherently delightful about well-engineered mechanical projects that serve a purely whimsical purpose. This 3D-printable, modular train whistle lets makers swap resonant chambers on the fly to replicate historic steam whistle chimes.
items.summary: A clever 3D-printing project offers a modular 3-inch train whistle with adjustable bell caps to change resonant notes on the fly. By tweaking the chamber dimensions, makers can switch between authentic historic steam whistle chimes using common FDM printers.

items.title: The Invisible Lamplighter of The Hague
items.why: Hidden urban art pieces that celebrate forgotten historical professions are always worth highlighting. This charming bronze sculpture in The Hague captures a lamplighter mid-climb from an era before automated electricity took over.
items.summary: Tucked away in an alleyway in The Hague, a bronze sculpture titled De Lantaarnopsteker depicts a lamplighter scrambling up a lamp post. Created by Dutch sculptor Loek Bos, the artwork immortalizes the historic trade of manually lighting city streets before automated electricity.

items.title: MEUTE: The 11-Piece Techno Marching Band
items.why: Bridging the gap between electronic club music and traditional marching band instrumentation is a wonderfully eccentric creative pursuit. It is a refreshing antidote to algorithmic monotony.
items.summary: MEUTE is an 11-piece German marching band that swaps synthesizers and laptops for tubas, trombones, and drum kits to perform electronic music acoustically. Their unique arrangements bring a surprisingly rich physical energy to modern techno tracks.

items.title: Hot Jupiter Vanishes from Sight After Gravitational Tug from Unseen Neighbor
items.why: When a transiting exoplanet monitored by TESS for seven years suddenly stops showing up, it forces astronomers to look closer at orbital dynamics. This clear, source-backed finding explains how a neighboring giant planet can gravitationally tug a world right out of our line of sight.
items.summary: Astronomers analyzing seven years of TESS data discovered that a hot Jupiter about 1,000 light-years away stopped transiting its star. They determined that an unseen massive companion planet gravitationally tugged the world off its previous transit alignment.

items.title: This Smart Coffee Kiosk Is Now Playing DOOM
items.why: There is a wonderful, enduring hacker tradition of getting id Software's classic shooter running on anything with a microprocessor. This detailed teardown of a Linux-powered commercial coffee kiosk provides a clever look into embedded hacking and low-level debugging ports.
items.summary: A hardware hacker managed to run DOOM on the i.MX 6 ARM Cortex-A9 processor powering a commercial self-serve coffee kiosk's touchscreen module. By probing the debug port on the machine's smart controller, they added a whole new kind of hard mode to your morning caffeine run.

items.title: A Local Browser Tool for Tracking Overhead Satellites and Imagery
items.why: With modern skies growing crowded with constellations, open-source utilities that let developers run SGP4 orbital mechanics locally in the browser are fantastic. It is a neat engineering project that highlights how everyday observers can monitor passing hardware and downlinked data.
items.summary: A developer has built a browser-based satellite tracker using simplified perturbation models to map passes over any location in real time. The open-source tool runs entirely client-side and can automatically pull imagery transmitted by passing spacecraft.

items.title: Voyager 1 Reaches One Light-Day Distance from Earth
items.why: Reaching a distance where radio signals take 24 hours to make a one-way trip is a mind-boggling milestone for humanity's most distant emissary. NASA's celebration of Voyager 1's historic 50-year journey offers a wonderful moment to reflect on interstellar operations.
items.summary: Nearly 50 years after its launch in 1977, Voyager 1 is set to cross the one light-day distance threshold, sitting more than 16 billion miles away from Earth. NASA is marking the historic interplanetary milestone with public engagement events and global participation.

items.title: First Direct Measurement of Cosmic Hydrogen Mapping the Universe
items.why: Radio astronomy breakthroughs that give us a new handle on large-scale cosmic structure are always worth highlighting. The MeerKLASS collaboration's work offers a concrete look at how direct hydrogen mapping will change cosmological surveys.
items.summary: The international MeerKLASS collaboration has achieved the first direct measurement of the large-scale clustering of cosmic hydrogen in the universe. The breakthrough technique promises to open new ways for astronomers to map cosmic structure and galaxy evolution.

items.title: Announcing .NET 11
items.why: The latest major .NET release has arrived with hundreds of runtime performance boosts, C# language updates, and enhanced tooling. It is a Standard Term Support release aimed at making cross-platform and cloud development smoother.
items.summary: Microsoft officially launched .NET 11, bringing speed improvements across C# 15, ASP.NET Core, and .NET MAUI. The new version features streamlined SDK tooling and expanded capabilities for agentic and AI-assisted development workflows.

items.title: .NET and .NET Framework November 2026 Servicing Updates
items.why: Staying on top of monthly servicing releases is essential for maintaining production security across multiple target frameworks. This month addresses key elevation of privilege and denial of service vulnerabilities.
items.summary: Microsoft released its November 2026 security and non-security updates for .NET 8, 9, 10, and 11. Administrators should review the advisories for CVE-2026-114146 and related patches to apply necessary remediation guidance.

items.title: Automated Assembly in Space Is the Future and NOM4D Is Showing the Way
items.why: Moving past pre-constructed station modules requires entirely new robotic assembly techniques for large structures in orbit. Programs like NOM4D are proving that simple automated systems can successfully build trusses from component parts.
items.summary: A new space construction program called NOM4D demonstrated that autonomous robots can successfully assemble truss-like structures in space using premade components. This milestone marks a step forward in our ability to fabricate large infrastructure directly in orbit.

items.title: NASA Scientists Show How Gravitational Waves Can Reveal New Worlds
items.why: Combining gravitational wave astronomy with exoplanet hunting opens up an entirely novel way to detect distant worlds. Upcoming observatories like LISA could soon spot planets orbiting tightly bound white dwarf systems thousands of light-years away.
items.summary: Recent studies led by NASA astrophysicists detail how the upcoming LISA gravitational wave observatory could detect exoplanets throughout our galaxy. By analyzing how a planet modifies gravitational wave signals from orbiting white dwarfs, astronomers can spot unseen worlds.

items.title: Rigel and the Witch Head Nebula
items.why: Reflection nebulae illuminated by bright supergiants always provide stunning visual targets for astrophotographers. IC 2118 near Rigel offers a classic case of pareidolia coupled with intricate interstellar dust structures.
items.summary: An astrophotograph captures IC 2118, a faint reflection nebula known popularly as the Witch Head Nebula due to its uncanny resemblance to a caricature. Illuminated by the bright blue supergiant Rigel, the sprawling dust cloud spans about 50 light-years.

items.title: M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything Wins the Booker Prize
items.why: It is a rare and welcome event when uncompromising speculative fiction takes home a major mainstream literary prize like the Booker. M. John Harrison's win is a brilliant milestone for imaginative storytelling.
items.summary: M. John Harrison’s post-apocalyptic sci-fi novel The End of Everything has won the prestigious Booker Prize. Set in a bleak, post-collapse England, the book's victory has been widely celebrated across the science fiction community.

items.title: Do AI Coding Agents Care About SemVer?
items.why: This is a clever piece of practical engineering research that tests an assumption about how autonomous agents interact with codebases. It turns out that version numbers still act as a subtle psychological nudge even for LLMs.
items.summary: Microsoft researchers tested whether AI coding agents pay attention to semantic versioning when upgrading dependencies. Surprisingly, experiments revealed that version numbers alone changed how models handled byte-identical code modifications.
